subject: botany_2
question_text: Do you think Mendel's laws of inheritance would have been different if the characters he chose were located on the same chromosome?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.42, printed question 83. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Answer YES, then name the law that would have failed. Naming independent assortment specifically is what earns the second mark.

steps.label: The answer
steps.margin_note: Yes plus the named law. Three lines.
lines: YES. Mendel's laws would have been different.
steps.why: Only one of the three laws depends on the genes being on different chromosomes, so the answer has to name which one.
common_mistakes: Answering with a bare 'yes'. The mark is for naming which law fails.
Saying all three laws would fail. Segregation and dominance still hold for linked genes.
steps.memory_tip: Only independent assortment depends on separate chromosomes.

steps.label: The reason
steps.margin_note: Say inherited together, name linkage, and state the consequence.
lines: Genes located on the SAME chromosome are
inherited TOGETHER, because they travel together
They are called LINKED genes, and the phenomenon
So they do not assort independently.
steps.why: A chromosome moves as one piece at meiosis, so genes riding on it cannot be separated except by crossing over.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the word 'together'. The guide's own sentence drops it and reads as a fragment; inherited TOGETHER is the point.
Not naming linkage. It is the term for this.
